## make a simple regression model

```{r}
bears <- read.csv(file="BEARS.csv",header = TRUE)
#adjust factors to be factors
bears$SEX<- as.factor(bears$SEX)
bears$MONTH<- as.factor(bears$MONTH)
```

## Model LENGTH ~ NECK  this is an example  


Compare all models that predict LENGTH other than NECK.  
Then order them from worst to best by its value of Adjusted-Rsquared (bigger is better), or by RSE (residual standard error) where smaller is better. 

We, the master RStudio statisticians of this class are trying to organize bear size in a ranking of 4 different models comparing different bodily features. The data comes from the bears data package.

We will create a ranking using both residual standard error and adjusted R-squared.

LENGTH is numerical.

HEADLEN is numerical.

HEADWTH is numerical.

CHEST is numerical.

WEIGHT is numerical.

## Model LENGTH ~ HEADLEN

```{r}
plot(LENGTH~HEADLEN,data=bears, pch=15)
```

The plot suggests that as LENGTH increases, HEADLEN increases in a linear fashion.

```{r}
model.1 <- lm(LENGTH~HEADLEN,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.1)
```

The residual standard error is 4.235. Or 4.2 rounded.
The adjusted R-squared is 0.8434. Or 0.84 rounded.

## Model LENGTH ~ HeadWTH

```{r}
plot(LENGTH~HEADWTH,data=bears, pch=15)
```

The plot suggests that as LENGTH increases, HEADWTH increases, in a moderately linear fashion.

```{r}
model.2 <- lm(LENGTH~HEADWTH,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.2)
```

The residual standard error is 7.32.
The adjusted R-Squared is 0.5321. Or 0.53 rounded.

## Model LENGTH ~ CHEST

```{r}
plot(LENGTH~CHEST,data=bears, pch=15)
```

The plot suggests that as LENGTH increases, CHEST increases in a linear fashion.

```{r}
model.3 <- lm(LENGTH~CHEST,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.3)
```

The residual standard error is 4.939. Or 4.3 rounded.
The adjusted R-squared is 0.7869. Or 0.8 rounded.

## Model LENGTH ~ WEIGHT

```{r}
plot(LENGTH~WEIGHT,data=bears, pch=15)
```

The plot suggests that as LENGTH increases, WEIGHT increases in a nonlinear moderate curve.

```{r}
model.4 <- lm(LENGTH~WEIGHT,data=bears)
summary.lm(model.4)
```

The residual standard error is 5.432. Or 5.4 rounded.
The adjusted r-squared is 0.7423. or 0.74 rounded.

# CONCLUSIONS

To arrange the four models in a regression, we can use residual standard error which is numbered large to small. Adjusted R-squared is small to large.

Residual Standard Error:
Model 2 (7.32) - Model 4 (5.4) - Model 3(4.3) - Model 1 (4.2)

Adjusted R-Squared
Model 2 (0.53) - Model 4 (0.74) - Model 3 (0.8) - Model 1 (0.84)
